pr_title: sql/pgwire: fix race condition with default_int_size
pr_body:
fixes https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/issues/69451

The default_int_size session variable needs to be read in a different
goroutine from the session itself. It's read at parsing time, when
reading from the pgwire stmtBuf, but is written in the session.

This was a race condition. Now, the value is changed atomically
using a callback.

Release justification: bug fix for new feature
Release note: None
pr_comments: This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/cockroachdb/cockroach/69543)

> looks like this would prevent SET LOCAL default_int_size = x from working due to the way we treat callbacks (i.e. we don't "uncall" the callback when SET LOCAL completes), maybe we should block default_int_size from working with LOCAL?.

ah yeah... or add something similar to what you did for onApplicationNameChange where we check if it unchanged

banning `default_int_size` from SET LOCAL seems like a good idea all around. then we can keep `GetUnqualifiedIntSize` but  change it so it only looks at the `sessionDataStack.Base()`. (and use atomic.Load/Store)

thinking about this more, i think the change LGTM besides the Clone() thing and the reset thing after SET LOCAL.
you can probably remove the `skip.UnderRace(t, "See #69451")` as well.
@otan ok, should be ready to review now!

issue_context.title: pgwire: reading default_int_size can be racy
issue_context.body:
Setting `default_int_size` can potentially race with a pgwire race. Consider the sequence of steps:

* Run as a query `Query {"String": "SET default_int_size = 4"}`
* Send `Parse {"Query": "SELECT generate_series(1, 10)"}`

The second statement involves reading `default_int_size` off the `SessionData` from here: https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/16a8354aa86ff993846dda30f9b08729454fe1f8/pkg/sql/pgwire/conn.go#L434

However, the first statement still has to finish processing in `processCommandsAsync` for the latter to correct:
https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/16a8354aa86ff993846dda30f9b08729454fe1f8/pkg/sql/pgwire/conn.go#L298

However, if `SET default_int_size` is stalled and doesn't finish executing in `processCommandsAsync` before we read `PARSE` from the buffer, `PARSE` can use the old `default_int_size` value before it was set. However, we expect the `SET` to have already been completed before doing this. This causes the race.

# Further exacerbation

This is going to be further exacerbated by the implementation of `SET LOCAL`. Now, the race happens on the stack level because of the read of `UnqualifiedIntSize`. This happens when a begin query races against a parse:

# Workaround

The workaround for this is to WaitForQuery when doing a `SET` of the `default_int_size`. This is an example of doing that: https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/pull/69224/commits/57422100a7b23c3f64ab4c505e4ee1475f4aac19

# Repro

See #69448, run with `go test ./pkg/sql -run TestUnqualifiedIntSizeRace -test.v -race -count 30` 
```

func TestUnqualifiedIntSizeRace(t *testing.T) {
	defer leaktest.AfterTest(t)()
	defer log.Scope(t).Close(t)

	ctx := context.Background()

	const (
		// select generates 10 rows of results which the test retrieves using ExecPortal
		selectStmt = "SELECT generate_series(1, 10)"

		// stmtBufMaxLen is the maximum length the statement buffer should be during
		// execution
		stmtBufMaxLen = 2

		// The name of the portal, used to get a handle on the statement buffer
		portalName = "C_1"
	)

	// This buffer is necessary for some reason.
	var stmtBuff *sql.StmtBuf
	s, _, _ := serverutils.StartServer(t, base.TestServerArgs{
		Knobs: base.TestingKnobs{
			SQLExecutor: &sql.ExecutorTestingKnobs{
				// get a handle to the statement buffer during the Bind phase
				AfterExecCmd: func(_ context.Context, cmd sql.Command, buf *sql.StmtBuf) {
					switch tcmd := cmd.(type) {
					case sql.BindStmt:
						if tcmd.PortalName == "C_1" {
							stmtBuff = buf
						}
					default:
					}
				},
			},
		},
		Insecure: true,
	})
	defer s.Stopper().Stop(ctx)

	// Connect to the cluster via the PGWire client.
	p, err := pgtest.NewPGTest(ctx, s.SQLAddr(), security.RootUser)
	require.NoError(t, err)

	require.NoError(t, p.SendOneLine(`Query {"String": "SET default_int_size = 8"}`))
	require.NoError(t, p.SendOneLine(`Query {"String": "SET default_int_size = 4"}`))
	require.NoError(t, p.SendOneLine(`Parse {"Query": "SELECT generate_series(1, 10)"}`))
	require.NoError(t, p.SendOneLine(`Bind {"DestinationPortal": "C_1"}`))

	// wait for ready
	for i := 0; i < 2; i++ {
		until := pgtest.ParseMessages("ReadyForQuery")
		_, err = p.Until(false /* keepErrMsg */, until...)
		require.NoError(t, err)
	}

	_ = stmtBuff
}
```

# Future?

I think we should not allow `default_int_size` to be a session variable. It should be a cluster setting, with a fixed value on initialization of the pgwire connection.
comments: I confirmed that release-21.1 is affected. It's likely a bug ever since `default_int_size` was added.

Synthesizing some options from a discussion in Slack: https://cockroachlabs.slack.com/archives/CV581CE78/p1630087934008800

1. make default_int_size a cluster setting instead of a session setting (would be backwards incompatible)
2. add synchronization specifically on `default_int_size` changes 
3. add synchronization on **all** `sessionData` changes
4. have a copy of the `default int size` that's owned by the pgwire handler that is itself synchronized, and is copied to from the session when the session is done changing it
5. have a contract that you have to access DefaultIntSize on the session data with atomics.Load/Store
We can also deprecate the session variable entirely and rely on the cluster setting instead. Seems crazy this can be changed within a session. No deprecation cycle needed here!
I'm marking this is a GA blocker for 21.2 since the SET LOCAL changes (SessionDataStack) makes it much easier to hit this.

> stop using a session setting for default_int_size. @otan
<https://github.com/otan> could you explain a bit more why it's backward
compatible to start ignoring the session setting?

It's only backwards incompatible if we remove the cluster setting as well.
If we do this we still need it to be the cluster setting BUT we have to now
allow using SET default_int_size so it can't be modified during a session.

I have another fix in mind - make the session Data Stack only return the
bottom element for this read (and also for
https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/issues/69508 )  to avoid this race
condition. I'll get to it on Monday.
